cli.help: mcp-pubcheck {version} - compare built MCP server packages with server.json before you publish (offline).
--artifacts <dir|file>  Where the built packages are (repeatable): .tgz, .whl, .tar.gz, .mcpb, Dockerfile
--dockerfile <file>     Dockerfile whose LABEL is checked (last stage)
--oci-inspect <file>    `docker inspect` JSON whose Config.Labels is checked
--repo-url <url>        Repository URL for the namespace check (default: server.json, then .git/config)
--schema <file>         Use another copy of the server.json JSON Schema
--require-all           Exit 1 when a package has no artifact to compare
--verbose               Also list the checks that passed
--lang <en|ko>          Output language (also: MCP_PUBCHECK_LANG, then LC_ALL / LC_MESSAGES / LANG)
Exit codes: 0 pass, 1 errors found (or warnings with --strict), 2 bad usage or unreadable input.
summary.verdict.pass: Safe to publish as far as these checks can tell.
summary.verdict.fail: Fix the errors above before you publish.
demo.intro: This is the bundled practice example (a release with mistakes planted on purpose), not your project.
demo.outro: Check your own server with: mcp-pubcheck server.json --artifacts dist/
demo.fixed-hint: The corrected version of this example passes: examples/fixed
input.unknown-artifact: cannot tell what kind of artifact this is: {file}. Use --npm, --wheel, --sdist, --mcpb, --dockerfile or --oci-inspect.
input.bad-inspect: {file} does not look like `docker inspect` output (no Config.Labels). Create it with: docker inspect IMAGE > inspect.json
serverjson.bad-utf8: {file} is not valid UTF-8. Save it as UTF-8.
serverjson.lone-surrogate: {file} contains an unpaired surrogate escape (line {line}, column {col}); the registry rejects it. Remove it or write the full character.
archive.gzip-corrupt: {file}: corrupt or truncated gzip data. Rebuild the artifact.
archive.tar-corrupt: {file}: corrupt tar archive ({detail}). Rebuild the artifact.
archive.tar-truncated: {file}: tar archive is truncated. Rebuild the artifact.
archive.tar-unsupported: {file}: unsupported tar entry type '{type}' (sparse or multi-volume). Rebuild with a standard tool.
archive.zip-corrupt: {file}: corrupt or truncated zip ({detail}). Rebuild the artifact.
archive.zip-encrypted: {file}: encrypted zip entries are not supported.
archive.zip-method: {file}: unsupported zip compression method {method} (only stored and deflate).
archive.npm-no-package-json: {file}: no package.json found inside the tarball. Is this an `npm pack` tarball?
archive.npm-bad-package-json: {file}: the package.json inside the tarball is not valid JSON.
archive.wheel-no-metadata: {file}: no .dist-info/METADATA found inside the wheel. Is this a wheel?
archive.sdist-no-pkginfo: {file}: no PKG-INFO found inside the sdist. Is this a Python source distribution?
f.schema.ok.msg: server.json passes the bundled JSON Schema.
f.schema.invalid.fix: Change the field so it matches the server.json schema (see docs/rules.md#schema).
f.schema-version.other.fix: Switch to the bundled schema version, or pass --schema with a copy of the one you use.
f.typo-key.found.msg: Unknown key '{key}'. The schema allows extra keys, so it is silently ignored.
f.version-range.latest.msg: version '{value}' is not a concrete version.
f.version-range.latest.fix: Use one exact version such as 1.2.3; the registry rejects 'latest'.
f.version-range.range.fix: Use one exact version such as 1.2.3; ranges (^, ~, x, >=) are rejected.
f.forbidden-field.found.fix: Remove '{field}'; the registry rejects it for {type} packages.
f.registry-base-url.disallowed.msg: registryBaseUrl {url} is not allowed for {type} packages.
f.registry-base-url.disallowed.fix: Use {allowed}, or remove the field. Private mirrors are not accepted.
f.meta-keys.dropped.msg: _meta keys are silently dropped when publishing: {keys}.
f.meta-keys.dropped.fix: Move the data you want to keep under '{kept}'.
f.meta-size.too-large.msg: The publisher-provided _meta is {bytes} bytes; the limit is {limit}.
f.meta-size.too-large.fix: Shrink it below {limit} bytes; publishing fails otherwise.
f.namespace-owner.ok.msg: Namespace owner matches the repository owner '{owner}'.
f.namespace-owner.mismatch.msg: Namespace '{namespace}' does not match the repository owner '{owner}'.
f.namespace-owner.mismatch.fix: Rename the server to io.github.{owner}/..., or publish from the account that owns the namespace.
f.namespace-owner.case.msg: Namespace owner differs from '{owner}' only by letter case; the registry compares it case-sensitively.
f.version-drift.ok.msg: packages version equals the server.json version.
f.version-drift.drift.msg: packages[{index}].version is {actual} but server.json version is {top}.
f.version-drift.drift.fix: Make both equal. The registry does not compare them, and `jq '.version = $v'` changes only the top-level one.
f.npm-identifier.ok.msg: Tarball package name matches the identifier.
f.npm-identifier.mismatch.msg: {file}: package name is {actual}, but the identifier is {expected}.
f.npm-identifier.mismatch.fix: Fix packages[].identifier or the name in package.json, then run npm pack again.
f.npm-version.mismatch.msg: {file}: the tarball contains version {actual}, but server.json expects {expected}.
f.npm-version.mismatch.fix: Bump package.json and run npm pack again, or update server.json. Do not publish this tarball.
f.npm-mcp-name.ok.msg: Tarball mcpName matches the server name.
f.npm-mcp-name.missing.msg: {file}: the packed package.json has no mcpName.
f.npm-mcp-name.missing.fix: Add "mcpName": "{expected}" to package.json and pack again. Check that no prepack script rewrites it.
f.npm-mcp-name.mismatch.msg: {file}: mcpName is {actual}, but the server name is {expected}.
f.npm-mcp-name.mismatch.fix: Set mcpName to exactly {expected} and pack again.
f.npm-mcp-name.case.msg: {file}: mcpName {actual} differs from {expected} only by letter case.
f.npm-mcp-name.case.fix: The registry compares case-sensitively. Set mcpName to exactly {expected}.
f.pypi-name.mismatch.msg: {file}: distribution name is {actual}, but the identifier is {expected}.
f.pypi-name.mismatch.fix: Fix packages[].identifier or [project] name in pyproject.toml.
f.pypi-version.mismatch.msg: {file}: the wheel contains version {actual}, but server.json expects {expected}.
f.pypi-version.mismatch.fix: Rebuild after bumping the version in pyproject.toml, or update server.json.
f.sdist-version.mismatch.msg: {file}: the sdist contains version {actual}, but server.json expects {expected}.
f.sdist-version.mismatch.fix: Rebuild after bumping the version, or update server.json.
f.pypi-mcp-name.ok.msg: The package description contains the mcp-name token.
f.pypi-mcp-name.glued.msg: {file}: the token is followed by '{char}', which the registry reads as part of the name.
f.pypi-mcp-name.glued.fix: End the line right after the name, or put a space (or an HTML comment close) after it: mcp-name: {name}
f.pypi-mcp-name.case-only.msg: {file}: the token matches the server name only when letter case is ignored.
f.pypi-mcp-name.case-only.fix: Write the name exactly as in server.json: mcp-name: {name}
f.pypi-mcp-name.spacing.msg: {file}: the name is there, but the spacing after 'mcp-name:' is not exactly one space.
f.pypi-mcp-name.different.msg: {file}: the token names {found}, but the server name is {name}.
f.pypi-mcp-name.missing.msg: {file}: the package description has no mcp-name token.
f.pypi-mcp-name.missing.fix: Add this line to your README and rebuild: mcp-name: {name}
f.pypi-mcp-name.no-readme.msg: {file}: the package metadata contains no README text at all, so the token cannot be found.
f.pypi-mcp-name.no-readme.fix: Set readme = "README.md" under [project] in pyproject.toml, put mcp-name: {name} in it, and rebuild.
f.mcpb-sha256.mismatch.fix: Set fileSha256 to {sha256}. A rebuilt bundle always has a new hash.
f.mcpb-url.ok.msg: MCPB URL is a release asset URL containing 'mcp'.
f.mcpb-url.bad.msg: The MCPB identifier is not a GitHub or GitLab release asset URL: {url}
f.mcpb-url.no-mcp.msg: The MCPB URL does not contain 'mcp': {url}
f.mcpb-url.no-mcp.fix: Name the release asset or repository so the URL contains 'mcp'.
f.mcpb-manifest.mismatch.msg: {file}: manifest.json version is {actual}, but server.json version is {expected}.
f.mcpb-manifest.mismatch.fix: Rebuild the bundle with the same version.
f.mcpb-manifest.unreadable.msg: {file}: manifest.json could not be read (not a zip, missing, or no version).
f.mcpb-manifest.unreadable.fix: Check the bundle was built with `mcpb pack`. The hash check still ran.
f.oci-label.ok.msg: Image label matches the server name.
f.oci-label.missing.fix: Add LABEL {label}="{expected}" to the last stage of the Dockerfile.
f.oci-label.mismatch.msg: {file}: label is {actual}, but the server name is {expected}.
f.oci-label.case.msg: {file}: label {actual} differs from {expected} only by letter case.
f.oci-label.case.fix: The registry compares case-sensitively. Use exactly {expected}.
f.oci-label.unresolved.msg: {file}: the label depends on an ARG/ENV value that cannot be resolved offline.
f.oci-label.unresolved.fix: Check the built image instead: docker inspect IMAGE > inspect.json, then pass --oci-inspect inspect.json.
f.oci-tag.mismatch.msg: The image tag is {actual}, but server.json version is {expected}.
f.oci-tag.mismatch.fix: Tag the image with the release version, or update the identifier.
f.oci-tag.missing.msg: The OCI identifier {identifier} has no tag.
f.oci-tag.missing.fix: Add an explicit tag such as :1.2.3. OCI packages carry the version in the identifier.
f.skipped.no-artifact.msg: No built {type} artifact found for {identifier}; nothing was compared.
f.skipped.no-artifact.fix: Pass --artifacts <dir> (or --npm, --wheel, --sdist, --mcpb, --dockerfile, --oci-inspect). Use --require-all to make this an error.
f.ambiguous.multiple.msg: More than one artifact could belong to this package: {files}
f.ambiguous.multiple.fix: Pass the exact file with --npm, --wheel, --sdist or --mcpb, or clean old builds from the directory.
f.no-packages.info.msg: server.json has no packages[]; only the server.json rules were checked.
